title: The Wall That Could Not Be Copied

source_links.title: ICOM Code of Ethics for Museums

fact_notes: ICOMが重視する文化財の保存と地域との協働という考えを参照。壁画と建物改修の事例は架空。
英文・全訳・設問・解説は独自制作。

sentences.en: A large mural covers the wall of a former railway building in a neighborhood undergoing rapid redevelopment.
sentences.ja: 急速に再開発が進む地域の旧鉄道建物の壁には、大きな壁画が描かれています。

sentences.en: The painting depicts residents carrying luggage, sharing food, and greeting one another at the station decades earlier.
sentences.ja: 絵には何十年も前の駅で荷物を運び、食べ物を分け合い、あいさつする住民が描かれています。

sentences.en: Many people regard the mural as a local landmark, although few remember exactly what the artist intended when painting it.
sentences.ja: 多くの人は壁画を地域の象徴と考えますが、作者が何を意図したか正確に覚えている人はほとんどいません。

sentences.en: The building's owner now proposes renovations that would improve entrances and make the space easier to use for people with limited mobility.
sentences.ja: 所有者は今、入口を改善し移動に制約のある人も使いやすくする改修を提案しています。

sentences.en: However, the plan requires removing part of the original painted wall, causing residents to disagree about what should be protected.
sentences.ja: しかしその計画は元の壁画の一部を取り除く必要があり、住民の間で何を守るべきか意見が分かれます。

sentences.en: Their dispute shows how a public work of art can connect private ownership with cultural meanings shared by many people.
sentences.ja: その対立は公共の芸術作品が個人の所有権と多くの人が共有する文化的意味を結びつける様子を示します。

sentences.en: At a community meeting, the first question concerns who has the authority to decide what happens to the mural.
sentences.ja: 地域の会議では、壁画をどうするか決める権限を誰が持つかが最初の問題になります。

sentences.en: Legal ownership gives the building owner important rights, but it does not erase the memories accumulated by people who encounter the painting every day.
sentences.ja: 法的所有は所有者に重要な権利を与えますが、毎日絵と出会う人々が積み重ねた記憶を消し去りません。

sentences.en: For example, older residents recall gathering beside the wall during celebrations, while young commuters associate it with ordinary journeys.
sentences.ja: 例えば年配の住民は祝いの場で壁のそばに集まったことを思い出し、若い通勤者は日常の移動と結びつけています。

sentences.en: Those experiences cannot automatically settle property law, yet they help explain why the image matters beyond its market value.
sentences.ja: その経験は財産法を自動的に解決しませんが、絵が市場価値以上に大切な理由を説明します。

sentences.en: A discussion limited to the owner's legal position would therefore overlook people whose lives have given the mural additional meaning.
sentences.ja: 所有者の法的立場だけに限った議論は、壁画に追加の意味を与えた人々を見落とすことになります。

sentences.en: Recognizing these voices does not mean granting every resident the right to demand an identical outcome.
sentences.ja: こうした声を認めることは、すべての住民に同じ結果を要求する権利を与えることではありません。

sentences.en: Some participants propose recording the mural digitally and displaying the image inside the renovated building.
sentences.ja: 参加者の中には壁画をデジタル記録し、改修後の建物内にその画像を展示することを提案する人もいます。

sentences.en: A detailed reproduction would allow former residents to view the artwork online and help researchers examine its visual features.
sentences.ja: 詳しい複製は元住民がオンラインで作品を見たり、研究者が視覚的特徴を調べたりする助けになります。

sentences.en: Nevertheless, a digital image cannot fully reproduce the experience of approaching a wall while walking through a familiar neighborhood.
sentences.ja: それでもデジタル画像は、見慣れた地域を歩いて壁に近づく体験を完全には再現できません。

sentences.en: Its colors and shapes can be recorded, but its surroundings, scale, and changing social uses are harder to preserve.
sentences.ja: 色や形は記録できても、周囲の環境、大きさ、変化する社会的な使われ方は保存しにくいのです。

sentences.en: A proposal to move the painted material itself raises different questions involving technical risk, expense, and possible damage.
sentences.ja: 絵が描かれた材料そのものを移す案は、技術的危険、費用、損傷の可能性という別の問題を生みます。

sentences.en: The meeting gradually recognizes that preserving an artwork, its physical location, and its public significance are connected but distinct goals.
sentences.ja: 会議では作品、物理的な場所、公共的な意味を守ることが結びついていても別々の目標だと次第に認識されます。

sentences.en: The organizers then invite people whose daily access to the building is limited by the old staircase and narrow entrances.
sentences.ja: 主催者は古い階段や狭い入口のために日常的な利用が制限されている人々を招きます。

sentences.en: These participants explain that preserving the wall without changing the entrance could maintain a different kind of exclusion.
sentences.ja: 参加者は入口を変えず壁だけ守れば、別の種類の排除を維持する可能性があると説明します。

sentences.en: Instead of choosing between perfect preservation and complete demolition, a designer offers a revised route that protects most of the artwork.
sentences.ja: 完全な保存か全面撤去かを選ぶのではなく、設計者は作品の大部分を守る改訂経路を示します。

sentences.en: Sections that cannot remain would be documented, and the reasons for altering them would be available to visitors.
sentences.ja: 残せない部分は記録され、変更の理由は訪問者が確認できるようになります。

sentences.en: The plan is more complicated than either extreme, but it acknowledges different forms of harm that the earlier debate ignored.
sentences.ja: その案はどちらの極端な案より複雑ですが、以前の議論が無視した異なる種類の害を認めています。

sentences.en: A creative compromise becomes possible when participants explain the concerns behind their positions rather than simply repeating demands.
sentences.ja: 参加者が要求を繰り返すのではなく、立場の背後にある懸念を説明すると創造的な妥協が可能になります。

sentences.en: Another question arises about whose version of the mural's history should be presented in the redesigned exhibition.
sentences.ja: 再設計された展示で誰の版の壁画の歴史を紹介すべきかという別の問いが生まれます。

sentences.en: The artist's original explanation matters, but the work has also become part of other people's memories over many years.
sentences.ja: 作者の最初の説明は重要ですが、作品は長年の間に他の人々の記憶の一部にもなってきました。

sentences.en: Students propose collecting short accounts from people who supported the renovation as well as those who opposed it.
sentences.ja: 生徒たちは改修を支持した人と反対した人の両方から短い証言を集めることを提案します。

sentences.en: However, selecting which stories to display creates a new responsibility because no exhibition can represent every possible perspective.
sentences.ja: しかし展示する話を選ぶことは新しい責任を生みます。すべての視点を代表できる展示はないからです。

sentences.en: The team records how contributors were invited and explains that additional accounts may lead to future changes.
sentences.ja: 担当者は協力者をどう招いたか記録し、追加の証言によって将来変更されるかもしれないと説明します。

sentences.en: Transparency cannot produce a complete history, but it helps visitors understand why an account remains open to revision.
sentences.ja: 透明性は完全な歴史を作れませんが、なぜ説明が修正に開かれているかを訪問者が理解する助けになります。

sentences.en: When the building reopens, most of the mural remains beside the new entrance, while a digital record shows the altered sections.
sentences.ja: 建物が再開すると壁画の大部分は新しい入口の隣に残り、変更部分はデジタル記録で示されます。

sentences.en: Some residents remain disappointed, since every compromise may involve losses that matter deeply to particular people.
sentences.ja: どんな妥協にも特定の人にとって大切な損失が伴い得るため、落胆したままの住民もいます。

sentences.en: As a result, the organizers promise to review the project rather than treating reopening day as the end of discussion.
sentences.ja: そこで主催者は再開日を議論の終わりとするのではなく、事業を見直すと約束します。

sentences.en: The case suggests that cultural stewardship does not always mean keeping every physical detail unchanged at any cost.
sentences.ja: この事例は、文化を守ることがどんな犠牲を払っても物理的な細部を一切変えないこととは限らないと示します。

sentences.en: It may instead require explaining difficult trade-offs and taking seriously the experiences of people who value the same place differently.
sentences.ja: むしろ難しい利害調整を説明し、同じ場所に異なる価値を見いだす人々の経験を真剣に扱うことが必要かもしれません。

sentences.en: The wall could be legally owned by one person yet carry memories shared by hundreds, and neither fact makes the other irrelevant.
sentences.ja: 壁は法的には一人の所有でも、何百人もの共有の記憶を持つことがあり、どちらの事実も他方を無関係にはしません。

questions.prompt: What conflict begins the discussion about the mural?
options: The museum has lost the mural entirely.
The artist wants to close the railway.
Every resident agrees about renovation.
Improving access may require removing some of the painting.
questions.explanation_ja: 第1段落の「しかしその計画は元の壁画の一部を取り除く必要があり、住民の間で何を守るべきか意見が分かれます。」が判断の根拠です。

questions.prompt: Why is ownership alone not the whole issue?
options: Property law is never relevant to buildings.
Every resident painted an equal part of the mural.
Many residents have cultural memories connected to the work.
The building has no legal owner.
questions.explanation_ja: 第2段落の「法的所有は所有者に重要な権利を与えますが、毎日絵と出会う人々が積み重ねた記憶を消し去りません。」が判断の根拠です。

questions.prompt: What does the author illustrate with older and younger residents?
options: All generations remember the artist's original explanation.
The artwork carries different memories for different people.
Only older people appreciate any art.
The mural depicts their exact daily experiences.
questions.explanation_ja: 第2段落の「例えば年配の住民は祝いの場で壁のそばに集まったことを思い出し、若い通勤者は日常の移動と結びつけています。」が判断の根拠です。

questions.prompt: What limitation of digital reproduction is emphasized?
options: It cannot fully capture the original encounter with a place.
It cannot record the painting's colors.
Digital images are always illegal.
Online access prevents historical research.
questions.explanation_ja: 第3段落の「それでもデジタル画像は、見慣れた地域を歩いて壁に近づく体験を完全には再現できません。」が判断の根拠です。

questions.prompt: What forms of preservation are distinguished?
options: Saving only the color of the wall.
Preserving digital files and deleting every building.
Protecting solely the owner's financial return.
Saving the artwork, its setting, and its public meaning.
questions.explanation_ja: 第3段落の「会議では作品、物理的な場所、公共的な意味を守ることが結びついていても別々の目標だと次第に認識されます。」が判断の根拠です。

questions.prompt: How does the designer avoid the original two extremes?
options: By moving every historical object abroad.
By refusing to discuss preservation.
By changing the entrance route while protecting much of the mural.
By banning people with mobility needs.
questions.explanation_ja: 第4段落の「完全な保存か全面撤去かを選ぶのではなく、設計者は作品の大部分を守る改訂経路を示します。」が判断の根拠です。

questions.prompt: What makes a creative compromise more possible?
options: Choosing only the cheapest proposal.
Explaining reasons behind preferences.
Repeating demands without listening.
Ignoring people affected by entrances.
questions.explanation_ja: 第4段落の「参加者が要求を繰り返すのではなく、立場の背後にある懸念を説明すると創造的な妥協が可能になります。」が判断の根拠です。

questions.prompt: Why must exhibition organizers be careful in selecting accounts?
options: No display can fully represent every viewpoint.
Every account from the artist is false.
Only one resident has a memory.
Community stories cannot be recorded.
questions.explanation_ja: 第5段落の「しかし展示する話を選ぶことは新しい責任を生みます。すべての視点を代表できる展示はないからです。」が判断の根拠です。

questions.prompt: Why might some people remain dissatisfied?
options: The renovation never took place.
Every participant preferred the final plan.
The original wall was never valued.
Compromise involves losses important to individuals.
questions.explanation_ja: 第6段落の「どんな妥協にも特定の人にとって大切な損失が伴い得るため、落胆したままの住民もいます。」が判断の根拠です。

questions.prompt: Which best summarizes the writer's conclusion?
options: A digital reproduction always replaces a public artwork perfectly.
Preservation should always prevent accessibility changes.
Cultural stewardship requires openness about trade-offs and different forms of belonging.
Legal ownership automatically resolves all cultural conflicts.
questions.explanation_ja: 第6段落の「むしろ難しい利害調整を説明し、同じ場所に異なる価値を見いだす人々の経験を真剣に扱うことが必要かもしれません。」が判断の根拠です。

grammar.focus: causing residents to disagree about what should be protected
grammar.explanation_ja: 分詞構文が計画の結果を示します。

grammar.explanation_ja: 関係代名詞whoがpeopleを修飾します。

grammar.focus: Instead of choosing between perfect preservation and complete demolition
grammar.explanation_ja: instead of + 動名詞が二者択一との対比を示します。

grammar.focus: does not always mean keeping every physical detail unchanged
grammar.explanation_ja: does not alwaysは必ずしもそうではないという部分否定です。

discourse.role_ja: 逆接：利用しやすさの改善と壁画の一部撤去という問題を示します。
例示：世代ごとの記憶の違いを示します。

帰結：妥協後も再検討を続けることにします。

paraphrases.source: Their dispute shows how a public work of art can connect private ownership with cultural meanings shared by many people.
paraphrases.rewrite: The mural connects private ownership with memories shared across the community.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 個人の所有権と共有された記憶の関係を表します。

paraphrases.source: Recognizing these voices does not mean granting every resident the right to demand an identical outcome.
paraphrases.rewrite: Hearing community voices does not give everyone a right to demand the same outcome.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 声を認めることと同じ結果を要求できることを区別します。

paraphrases.source: The plan is more complicated than either extreme, but it acknowledges different forms of harm that the earlier debate ignored.
paraphrases.rewrite: The compromise recognizes several harms that earlier proposals overlooked.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 複数の害を考慮する案という意味です。

paraphrases.source: It may instead require explaining difficult trade-offs and taking seriously the experiences of people who value the same place differently.
paraphrases.rewrite: Cultural protection may require negotiating difficult losses rather than avoiding all change.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 保護には変更を一切避ける以外の方法があるという主旨です。
